title: A caption pill lands where you let go of it
goal: Drag an arrow's label pill somewhere and let go: a short label lands about a centimetre from where you dropped it, because the app works out the drop using a guess at how wide the pill is rather than measuring it. Short labels are the ones people use most, so this is the case it gets most wrong.
notes: Found on 2026-09-05 while fixing the tail-meets-pill geometry. AnnotationBuilder.placingCaption converts the dropped CENTRE into the stored attachment with CaptionPlanner.attachment(forPillCenter:of:size:) passing a.estimatedCaptionSize, but the rasterizer hangs the MEASURED pill (CaptionMetrics.pillSize) off that attachment. For "ok" the estimate is 63pt wide and the measurement 44, so the pill lands (63-44)/2 = 9.5pt back toward the tail. The same guess drives CaptionPlanner.keepingOnCanvas and plan(). The fix is to let the app pass the measured size in, since only PhotonzRender can measure type: give placingCaption and planningCaption an optional pill size and thread CaptionMetrics.pillSize from EditorState (call sites around EditorState.swift 1241, 1281, 1308, 1325, 1350, 6292, 6616, 6667). Layer.drawnBounds already takes the measured pill this way.
acceptance: Dropping a pill anywhere puts its centre within a point of where you let go, for a two-letter label and a long one
The pill still holds that spot when the arrow is later moved or its ends dragged
A scripted walk drops a short label at a named point and the log shows the pill centred there

log.note: Adversarial review before building, with numbers from a scratch test against the real text measurer. (1) The reported symptom does NOT reproduce in open canvas: the drag takes its grip against the ESTIMATED pill centre and placingCaption converts back with the same estimate, so the two errors cancel and the pill tracks the pointer exactly. Verified: drop asked for (468.5, 240), pill drawn at (472.5, 240) relative to a grab that was itself 4pt off. Net miss 0.0. (2) The same mismatch is very visible at the edges of the picture, which is where redliners put labels. keepingOnCanvas slides a pinned pill back on using the oversized estimate, so a 25 character caption let go with its right edge 6pt inside the canvas lands 157pt further left, with a 163pt gap between the label and the edge it was aimed at. That is the real bug and it is worth fixing. (3) The same estimate is the pill's GRAB box, so up to 163pt of blank canvas past the label picks the label up ('Primary action' = 95pt, 'Save' = 28pt). (4) The estimate is 1.78pt SHORT in height for every caption, which contradicts its own comment claiming the drawn pill always sits inside it. Shortest version that delivers the value: thread the measured pill through the three things a person can see (where a drop lands, where the edge clamp pulls it to, where you can grab it) and leave frame reservation generous, since the frame also has to hold the shadow.

Out of scope, filed separately: Layer.contains(canvasPoint:) also hit-tests the caption with the estimate, so clicking blank canvas past a label selects the arrow. Fixing that means threading a measurement through Document.hitTest, a much wider change than this task.

Built. PhotonzCore now takes an optional MEASURED pill everywhere the placement is something a hand can feel: AnnotationBuilder.placingCaption/planningCaption/releasingCaption(captionPillSize:), CaptionPlanner.keepingOnCanvas(pillSize:), CanvasGrab.captionPillRect/hit(captionPillSize:) and CanvasPointerCue.cue(captionPillSize:). Nil keeps the old estimate, so frame reservation and the pure model are untouched. The app threads CaptionMetrics.pillSize through a new Layer.measuredCaptionPillSize (Sources/Photonz/CaptionPillSizing.swift) at every drop, re-plan, endpoint drag, whole-arrow move, font-size commit, grab box and pointer cue, and the playtest log now prints the pill centre at its measured width.

Verified in the real app, not just in tests. Scripts/playtest/caption-drop-lands-walk.json on the probe: a two letter label picked up by its middle and let go at (500, 700) logs 'pill (500, 700)' exactly; shoved past the right edge of a 1440 wide picture it logs 'pill (1413, 700)', which puts its right edge on 1440; a 25 character label shoved at the same edge logs 'pill (1318, 760)', right edge on 1440, where it used to stop at 1154 with 163pt of empty picture beyond it. Real window captures (Screen Recording granted) in queue/audits/2026-09-05-caption-drop-lands-*.png. 3622 tests green.

Adversarial review of the built thing: a label now allowed to touch the edge has its shadow and the outer half of its border clipped by the picture boundary, which is what dragging it there asks for but is worth a decision (raised in the audit's evaluate list). The grab box is now tight to the label plus the usual 6pt, which is honest but less forgiving than the accidental margin it had. Selection hit-testing still uses the estimate, filed as 'Clicking blank canvas next to a label does not select its arrow'.
